feed.title: NPR Topics: Climate
feed.subtitle: In-depth coverage of climate change, weather events, climate science, emissions targets and adaptation strategies from NPR’s climate reporters.

entry.title: China's emissions have plateaued — and may even be falling
entry.summary: China and the U.S. are the world's two largest emitters of planet-heating pollution. But experts say China's emissions are now plateauing.

entry.title: China and the U.S. are the world's biggest polluters. And the U.S. is falling behind
entry.summary: The two largest emitters of greenhouse gases are China and the United States. Now, the countries' stories are diverging: many Chinese provinces are reducing coal use, while the U.S. is falling behind on climate technologies.

entry.title: They tried to torture him into leaving Iraq. He refused to abandon the nature he protects
entry.summary: Iran-backed militias kidnapped and tortured him, but Jassim al-Asadi is still on a mission to save Iraq's marshes, and a way of life stretching back to the dawn of history.

entry.title: What influence does the U.S. have at this year's U.N. climate talks?
entry.summary: The U.S. isn't at the negotiating table at the UN climate conference but attendees are talking about the midterms. Democratic members Congress are vowing to undo actions by the Trump administration.

entry.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
entry.summary: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

entry.title: China's emissions have plateaued -- and may even be falling
entry.summary: China and the U.S. are the world's two largest emitters of planet-heating pollution. But experts say China's emissions are now plateauing.

entry.title: Rivers in the sky are raining down on the Pacific Northwest. What are they?
entry.summary: Atmospheric rivers are large bands of water vapor in the sky. They are dumping trillions of gallons of water on Washington and Oregon, just as high tides and winds batter shorelines.

entry.title: Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
entry.summary: Countries are not meeting their goal of limiting climate change to 1.5 degrees Celsius. How much hotter the planet gets makes a profound difference for the impacts the world could see.

entry.title: Leaders at the U.N. climate summit urged to get tougher on global warming
entry.summary: World leaders are gathered in Turkey for climate talks, after a year of conflict that has frayed international ties and upended global energy markets. One conspicuous absence: the U.S.

entry.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
entry.summary: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country.
